corrections.compiler_and_flags: C++ baseline: g++ 16.1.0 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wcast-align -O3 -march=native -flto=auto -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -std=c++23 (common/commands.mk GCC_CPP_BUILD, libstdc++); clang++ 22.1.8 row uses the same flags with -stdlib=libc++. corrections.caveats: Not the same algorithm: the C++/g++ baseline (brainfuck/bf.cpp) is a tree-walking interpreter that dispatches every Brainfuck instruction at run time, while the staged variant compiles the Brainfuck program to native code at run time; the suite's own brainfuck/README.md says implementations interpret every instruction one by one, so the staged rows deviate from the suite rule. The repository has no C or C++ staged/JIT counterpart, so the result shows runtime compilation beating an interpreter, not the language beating C++ at equal work. The timed region (between the notify calls) includes parsing and the run-time compile on both sides, but verify() runs one staged compile of a hello-world program before timing, warming the compiler machinery. Measurements run with QUIET=1 (analyze.rb, 10 attempts, median with MAD), so output flushing does not matter. Single machine (Xeon E-2324G), single suite. Wins only on bench.b (1.24x) and loses on mandel.b (15.722s vs 10.143s, 1.55x slower), so the bench.b win does not generalise; the bench.b margin is well outside the reported MADs on this machine. On bench.b C++/g++ is not the fastest AOT interpreter either (V/gcc 0.985s, Rust 1.008s, D/ldc2 1.078s). The generated code uses unsafe fixnum and vector operations (#%declare #:unsafe); bf.cpp also indexes std::vector without bounds checks, so safety checks are comparable.

notes: Numbers, flags, CPU and code all check out; downgraded A to C because the staged Racket row compiles the Brainfuck program with eval (Chez Scheme backend, PLT_CS_COMPILE_LIMIT=100000) while the C++ baseline interprets it, and the same-algorithm Racket row is 1.6x slower than C++. Not D: the C++ baseline is fully optimised (-O3 -march=native -flto), not crippled. Loses on mandel.b.
